prompt:
Write 10 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a rear-end collision claim, in time order. Injury: knee injury. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1158; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The claimant later added small details, but the account stayed the same.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened after a rear-end collision reported by the insured driver. The claimant is represented by counsel, and all further contact is being routed through the attorney's office.

Entry 2: Police report and two independent witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle at the time of impact. The other driver's statement describes the collision the same way the claimant does.

Entry 3: Photos from the scene and the other driver's account are consistent with the rear-end impact as described. Damage to the claimant's vehicle lines up with the reported force of the collision.

Entry 4: Confirmed the driver is named on the policy and that coverage was in force on the date of loss. Nothing in the file suggests the damage predates the policy start.

Entry 5: Claimant reports a knee injury from the impact. The reported injury fits the kind and force of the crash, and no earlier injury to the same area is known from prior records.

Entry 6: Vehicle inspection found no earlier damage to the claimant's vehicle. The repair estimate covers only damage tied to this impact.

Entry 7: Claimant's attorney submitted the medical file. Treatment followed a usual course for this type of injury and tapered off as the patient improved.

Entry 8: In a follow-up interview, the claimant added a few small details about the sequence of events. The core account of the collision has stayed the same since the first report.

Entry 9: Reviewed the witness statements, scene photos and the other driver's account together. All sources agree the accident happened as described.

Entry 10: Medical and repair documents are complete and consistent with the reported loss. File is moving toward settlement review with the attorney's office.
